result.title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
result.comment: Accepted at the AI4Mat Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations. MatterChat addresses this challenge using a large bridge module between a pretrained structural encoder and the LLM, together with a separate contrastive alignment stage. We instead ask whether this bridge can adaptively select and combine representations from multiple structural encoders according to the target property. We find that supervised and generative material encoders provide complementary information for property prediction. We found that, for Zatom-1, this information is not concentrated in the final layer. Instead, the most informative representations occur at different depths depending on the target property. This motivates Task-Conditioned Attention Fusion (TCAF), a lightweight attention-based bridge that uses task-conditioned latent queries to combine CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations. The bridge is trained directly on downstream prediction tasks, allowing representation selection and material-language alignment to be learned jointly without separate contrastive pretraining. Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperforms MatterChat, with up to 47.8% lower RMSE, while using substantially fewer trainable parameters and halving the overall training time. Further experiments incorporating UMA-S demonstrate TCAF's flexibility across encoder combinations, with the three-encoder configuration achieving the highest macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作针对材料科学多模态语言模型，发现监督式与生成式结构编码器信息互补且最有用的表示分布在不同的中间层，深度依目标性质而异，据此提出任务条件注意力融合桥（TCAF），用任务条件 latent queries 将 CHGNet 特征与 Zatom-1 的中间层表示送入 LLM，并与下游任务联合训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其任务条件 latent queries 对不同深度、不同编码器表示做自适应筛选与融合，可能为 LVR 中「多种 latent 假设与视觉证据筛选」及跨层信息选取提供可核查的方法线索；但研究对象是材料性质预测而非视觉推理，联系需较多迁移核查。
